StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

ShouldScaleInMultiplayer.rationale: Multiplayer-only scaling (MultiplayerScalingModel). Out of scope; the sim is single-player.

ModifyHpLostAfterOsty.issue: The formula is exact: `target != base.Owner -> amount`, `amount < 1m -> amount`, else `1m` (SlipperyPower.cs:19-30) vs powers.py:1520-1522. The BeforeOsty/AfterOsty phase collapse is already resolved as faithful by damage_pipeline (Osty redirection is waived, so its steps 8 and 11 fold into one call). What is left is that the sim runs ALL seven HP-loss modifiers in one registration-order chain where C# runs a BeforeOsty pass then an AfterOsty pass then an AfterOstyLate pass -- hook_dispatch gap G3, not re-verdicted. It matters for THIS power because HardenedShellPower is the only `ModifyHpLostBeforeOsty*` implementer in the game and must therefore run before this one, and min-then-cap is not cap-then-min; see audit/records/power/hardened_shell.json, where the ordering was EXECUTED and found to coincide today (sim order ['HardenedShellPower', 'TheBoot', 'TungstenRod']). DORMANT by that executed check. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterDamageReceived.issue: Right slot (AfterDamageReceived -> cmds.py:122, killing-blow guard on both sides) and the right condition in shape: `target == base.Owner && result.UnblockedDamage >= 1` vs `target is self.owner and amount >= 1`. The divergence is WHICH NUMBER is tested. C#'s `UnblockedDamage` is post-block but PRE-HP-loss-modifier, so the stack is consumed whenever any damage got through the block. The sim's `amount` is `hp_lost`, i.e. post-block AND post-`modify_hp_lost` (cmds.py:86 then :122) -- and this power's own cap is one of those modifiers. It still reaches 1, so a stack is consumed either way HERE; but with HardenedShellPower's cap (or a future 0-flooring modifier) on the same creature the sim can see 0 where C# sees a positive UnblockedDamage and so FAIL to consume a stack, making Slippery last longer in the sim. Same `hp_lost`-for-`UnblockedDamage` substitution as power/hardened_shell.json's AfterDamageReceived entry -- one mechanism, one verdict (rule 3). DORMANT: no ported creature carries both Slippery and a second HP-loss modifier. Third-file citations, not hashed here.
